title: All grant will-fruits; Amyraut denies will-command needed for assent
source_text: VII. Caeterum fidem salvificam ad voluntatem pertinere ratione multorum actuum & fructuum fidei annexorum, & eam concomitantium, nemo est inter Doctores Reformatos qui dubitet. An autem assensus ille quem Verbo Dei praebemus, ratione originis ad voluntatem pertineat, & censeri debeat a voluntate imperatus, inter eos omnes non habetur pro comperto. Saltem Moses Amyraldus istud non videtur fuisse concessurus. Nam Thesibus de Causa Fidei docet fidem necessario oriri & produci ex appulsu objecti, id est, doctrinae Evangelicae, ad intellectum rite affectum atque dispositum per immediatam Spiritus Sancti operationem: quemadmodum sensatio necessario sequitur ad praesentiam objecti sensibilis, si sensus organum naturae convenienter se habeat. Unde sequitur ad fidei actum a mente eliciendum nullum voluntatis imperium requiri.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover no Reformed Doctor doubts that saving faith belongs to the will by reason of many annexed acts and fruits concomitant with faith. But whether that assent which we give to God's Word belongs to the will by origin and ought to be counted as commanded by the will is not held settled among them all. At least Moses Amyraut does not seem to have been about to concede that. For in Theses on the Cause of Faith he teaches that faith necessarily arises and is produced from the object's impact — that is, of Gospel doctrine — upon an intellect duly affected and disposed by the Spirit's immediate operation: just as sensation necessarily follows the presence of a sensible object if the sense organ is naturally fit. Whence it follows that for eliciting faith's act from the mind no empire of the will is required.
pass_b_english: Reformed agree faith's fruits touch the will; they quarrel whether assent is will-commanded.
Amyraut: faith follows Spirit-disposed intellect like sensation follows a fit organ — no will-imperium needed.
